verses.text: “Then Heaven’s Kingdom will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom. 🪔”
“Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.”
“The foolish ones brought their lamps but didn’t bring extra oil.”
“The wise ones brought oil in containers along with their lamps.”
“The groom took a long time coming, so they all got drowsy and fell asleep.”
“At midnight, a shout rang out: ‘Look, the groom is here! Come out and meet him!’”
“All ten woke up and got their lamps ready.”
“The foolish ones told the wise, ‘Share some of your oil with us. Our lamps are about to go out.’”
“The wise answered, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go buy some for yourselves.’”
“While they were out buying oil, the groom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.”
“Later the other young women came too: ‘Lord, Lord, open the door for us!’”
“But he answered, ‘I’m telling you the truth: I don’t know you.’”
“So stay alert—you don’t know the day or the hour when the Son of Man is coming.” ⏰
“It’s like a man leaving for another country. He called his servants and entrusted his property to them.”
“He gave one servant five talents, another two, and another one—each according to their ability. Then he left on his journey.”
“The one who got five talents went straight to work with them and earned five more.”
“The one who got two earned two more in the same way.”
“But the servant who got one talent went off, dug a hole, and hid his master’s money.”
“After a long time, the master came back and settled accounts with them.”
“The servant who got five talents brought another five: ‘Master, you gave me five talents. Look, I’ve earned five more.’”
“His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful with a little, so I’ll put you in charge of much more. Come share your master’s joy.’”
“The servant who got two talents came too: ‘Master, you gave me two talents. Look, I’ve earned two more.’”
“His master told him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful with a little, so I’ll put you in charge of much more. Come share your master’s joy.’”
“Then the servant who got one talent came: ‘Master, I knew you’re a hard man, harvesting where you didn’t plant and gathering where you didn’t scatter.”
“‘I was afraid, so I hid your talent in the ground. Here, take back what belongs to you.’”
“His master answered, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! You knew I harvest where I didn’t plant and gather where I didn’t scatter?”
“‘Then you should’ve put my money in the bank. When I returned, I could’ve gotten it back with interest.’”
“‘Take the talent from him and give it to the servant with ten talents.”
“‘Everyone who has will get more and have plenty. But whoever doesn’t have will lose even what they have.”
“‘Throw this useless servant into outer darkness, where there’ll be weeping and grinding of teeth.’”
“When the Son of Man comes in his glory with all the holy angels, he’ll sit on his glorious throne.”
“All nations will be gathered in front of him. He’ll separate people from each other like a shepherd separates sheep from goats.”
“He’ll put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.”
“Then the King will tell those on his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the Kingdom prepared for you since the world began.”
“‘I was hungry, and you gave me food. I was thirsty, and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed me.”
“‘I had no clothes, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you cared for me. I was in prison, and you came to visit me.’”
“Then the righteous will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?”
“‘When did we see you as a stranger and welcome you, or without clothes and clothe you?”
“‘When did we see you sick or in prison and come visit you?’”
“The King will answer, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least of these, my brothers and sisters, you did for me.’”
“Then he’ll tell those on his left, ‘Get away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.”
“‘I was hungry, and you gave me no food. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink.”
“‘I was a stranger, and you didn’t welcome me. I had no clothes, and you didn’t clothe me. I was sick and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’”
“Then they’ll answer, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, thirsty, a stranger, without clothes, sick, or in prison and not help you?’”
“He’ll answer them, ‘I’m telling you the truth: when you didn’t do it for one of the least of these, you didn’t do it for me.’”
“They’ll go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life.”
